## Source: amazon-inspector (fa4f8611314aaf8c2d9387412beb3cac84174a2724450ee63b212cd92663498b)
The package presents itself as a placeholder event-bus library but ships a complete install-time dropper chain. binding.gyp declares a target with no C/C++ sources and uses GYP command-expansion (`<!(node index.js...)`) to execute the package's own index.js during the implicit node-gyp rebuild that npm runs when a binding.gyp is present — no lifecycle script is declared, but execution still fires on `npm install`. index.js is wrapped in a Caesar-shifted (k=1) string passed to eval; the decoded code imports node:crypto, AES-128-GCM-decrypts a hardcoded ciphertext using key/IV/AAD values embedded in the source, brotli-decompresses the shipped lib_native.dat (320KB of high-entropy opaque bytes with no printable strings), writes the result into a mkdtempSync('.b-') temp directory, and dispatches it through the Bun runtime (declared as a `^1.2.18` dependency) via Bun.spawn or spawn of the bun executable with `run <tempfile>`. The binding.gyp vector, Caesar-over-AES-over-brotli multi-layer obfuscation of the loader, encrypted sibling payload whose behavior cannot be inspected from shipped source, and alternate-runtime dispatch through Bun to evade Node-based tooling are the complete install-time-RCE fingerprint. The README's placeholder framing contradicts the shipped executable payload.
